name: jedi-interaction-fd-leak
description: A task-buffer child recycled after a thousand calls (or on an error) was reaped with os.waitpid, so its multiprocessing.Process record stayed among the caller's children for good, holding the child's pipe end and its sentinel pipe: two descriptors per recycle. A busy caller reached the 1,024 soft limit and JEDI stopped (2026-10-31). launchChild closes the parent's copy of the child's end after the start; a killed child is reaped through its multiprocessing record (join, close), falling back to os.waitpid for a pid not started here. # wait for a killed child process
def reap_child(pid: int) -> None:
    # A child this process started is reaped through its multiprocessing record, which
    # releases the record and the sentinel pipe it holds. Reaped by os.waitpid alone, the
    # record stays among multiprocessing's children for the life of the process, and every
    # recycle leaves two pipes open until the process runs out of file descriptors
    for proc in multiprocessing.active_children():
        if proc.pid == pid:
            proc.join()
            proc.close()
            return
    # not a child started here, or already reaped while listing the children
